text:
alyssa_sales: Quick heads-up — FinHealth is asking for APAC-only hosting for their POC + a clear list of subprocessors for any cross-border egress. They also want to know how our routing fallback behaves during region failure and whether that changes POC pricing. Can someone confirm what we can promise for the proof-of-concept?

michael_se: +1. Need to confirm two things: 1) can we pin their tenant to APAC region for the POC? 2) if we do failover, do we route to APAC hot-standby in another APAC region or fall back to EU?

alyssa_sales: They want APAC only — ideally Singapore primary, Tokyo standby. They asked about subprocessor list up-front for legal sec questionnaire.

tara_security: We can share the subprocessors list but must mark which ones handle customer data vs metadata. Also note that some cloud infra has global control planes (control plane metadata in US), we should call that out. I'll draft the security answer.

jules_ops: For the POC we can do tenant-region pinning into ap-southeast-1 (SG) with a regional hot-standby in ap-northeast-1 (TYO). Failover behavior: we support two policies — strict-geofence (reject requests outside pinned regions) or allowed-failover (route to standby region). Which does FinHealth want?

alyssa_sales: They prefer allowed-failover but only within APAC. They will not accept EU/US fallback. Is that supported?

michael_se: Yes — we can enforce a routing policy with allowed-regions = ["ap-southeast-1","ap-northeast-1"] and deny others. Example config we typically hand to customers:

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "finhealth-poc",
  "routing_policy": {
    "mode": "region_pin",
    "allowed_regions": ["ap-southeast-1","ap-northeast-1"],
    "failover": "route_to_standby"
  },
  "kms_key_scope": "regional"
}
```

michael_se: That config keeps traffic inside APAC. Our control plane might still contact central telemetry endpoints unless they opt for Private.

tara_security: Important: for the hosted POC we use these subprocessors: cloud infra (major provider in APAC), observability vendor (ingests metrics, can be configured to sample), and our logging/alerts provider. I can provide the vendor list and which datatypes they see. For absolute control (no cross-border metadata) we recommend Private deployment or a Dedicated cluster with regional KMS.

ivan_finance: Pricing note — restricting to APAC and adding regional standbys increases cost ~+12% (ops overhead + capacity reservation). If they want SLA-backed standby, that's an extra charge. If they accept best-effort standby, smaller uplift. I can get a POC quote once requirements locked.

alyssa_sales: The customer also asked if BYOK (bring-your-own-key) is supported in POC to satisfy crypto controls. Can we do BYOK for hosted?

tara_security: Hosted supports customer-managed keys via our KMS integration, but with some caveats: master key material can be BYOK but some key usage metadata is still seen by control plane. For air-gapped BYOK we need Private. I'll list caveats in the questionnaire answer.

michael_se: Operational checklist I recommend we share with FinHealth: 1) Target regions and allowed failover list 2) Subprocessor CSV 3) KMS mode (hosted-BYOK vs private) 4) POC duration and expected QPS 5) Data retention requirements

alyssa_sales: I'll send that checklist to the customer. Tara — can you drop the subprocessors + the standard wording about control-plane metadata? Need by EOD for their legal review.

tara_security: On it. Draft coming in ~90m.

jules_ops: Note re networking: if they require no cross-border egress at all, we need to confirm certificate vaulting and peering for RGW endpoints; will add networking caveats to checklist.

infra-bot: New ticket created: INFRA-2027 "FinHealth POC: APAC-only residency + subprocessor list" assigned to jules_ops, tara_security, michael_se.

alyssa_sales: Perfect — once we have the subprocessors + ops caveats and a POC quote from Ivan I'll forward to the customer. Thanks team :raised_hands:
